On-Chain Operator. Lesson 14.3, Operating procedures: multisig signing, change control, reviews. Navy and cyan. One idea at a time. You write it down. Education only.
You already have a playbook. Automation may watch it. Automation may not hold your keys.
Multisig signing procedure: every signer independently verifies the transaction (destination, amount, calldata) on their own device screen, not a shared screenshot.
Change control: new protocol, new chain, new strategy, or a cap change is written up (thesis, risk register row, size) and waits 24h before execution.
Separation: the person proposing a vault transaction isn't the only one approving it.
Review calendar: weekly books · monthly register · quarterly stress test and recovery drill · annual review (Module 13.5).
Work the example on paper. A 2-of-3 vault moves $40,000 to the operating wallet. Stamp it Example. It is not a level to copy onto a live position.

Work the example on paper. Signer 1 proposes; Signer 2 checks the destination against the allowlist and the amount against the ladder refill schedule on their hardware wallet screen, then signs. Stamp it Example. It is not a level to copy onto a live position.
Work the example on paper. Logged in the books with both names. Stamp it Example. It is not a level to copy onto a live position.
On the checklist, this line has to be true in writing: Signing procedure written for every signer. If you cannot write it, the line is open.
On the checklist, this line has to be true in writing: Change-control template and 24h rule. If you cannot write it, the line is open.
On the checklist, this line has to be true in writing: Review calendar set. If you cannot write it, the line is open.
Check yourself. 1. Why verify on your own device screen? The answer: Screens and screenshots can be faked; the hardware display shows what you're actually signing.
Check yourself. 2. What is change control for? The answer: Forcing new risks through thesis, register and a cooling-off period.
Check yourself. 3. How often is the stress test re-run? The answer: Quarterly, and after big changes.
By the end of this lesson, you'll be able to run your bank with procedures that prevent single-point mistakes.
